heading: 4.5 Objective Five: change in diagnostic confidence
objective: To assess changes in clinicians’ confidence before and after receiving MAS and hs-CRP information.
methods: The two confidence assessments were paired within each patient record on the original five-category ordinal scale. The stated study assumption is that one doctor assessed each patient twice and no doctor assessed more than one patient; clinician identifiers were not recorded, so this independence assumption cannot be verified. The exact two-sided paired sign test is primary because it uses direction without assuming equal category spacing. A conditional Wilcoxon signed-rank test is reported as a sensitivity analysis, assuming rankable category-code changes and symmetric independent differences under its null. Ten unchanged pairs are excluded only from the tested nonzero-change denominator. Original questionnaire verification of the information timing remains outstanding.
finalParagraph: Diagnostic confidence increased after MAS/hs-CRP information in most paired assessments. The findings apply to reported ordinal confidence and depend on the assumed independent clinician–patient pairing. They do not distinguish the effects of the both-positive and either-positive strategies or establish improved diagnostic accuracy.
